The narrator lives in a hall of residence (a student dormitory—the "hall"), which is in an apartment-style residential building. They went to the shared kitchen of the hall, which they (mis)called "the pantry." There they heated oil or fat in a pan on the stove as part of preparing a meal—a normal cooking act, not something burning or charred. The heated oil/fat gave off smoke. Because the smoke drifted within the kitchen area, it triggered the fire alarm located in that kitchen, and the alarm rang. There was no actual fire, and no drill, prank, or other person set it off—the smoke from ordinary cooking was the genuine cause. The twist is simply that the "pantry" was really the hall of residence's shared kitchen, and "my hall" was the dormitory itself.
